CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Qanun, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bireuen Regency.
2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

Article 18

1. The implementation of protection for women victims of violence as referred to in Article 9 letter h, in order to provide legal protection and/or health recovery.
2. Protection for women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal aid;
b. assistance after the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
d. health services.

Article 19

1. Every victim as referred to in Article 18 has the right to receive protection, information, integrated services, continuous handling up to the rehabilitation stage and confidential handling from individuals, groups or institutions both the Regency Government and the community.
2. In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as women.

Article 30

(1) Women's protection is implemented by integrating Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) and disaggregated databases, gender data and violence data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.

(2) The District Work Unit that handles women's empowerment and protection coordinates with other Regional Apparatus Organizations in order to realize the implementation of women's protection in an integrated manner.

(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2), is carried out within the framework of strengthening synergy in policy formulation, program and activity support, as well as monitoring and evaluation.

Article 22

1. The Regency Government has obligations and responsibilities for the protection of women.
2. Efforts to protect women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. Protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 13

1. Implementation of protection for women domestic workers as referred to in Article 9 letter c, in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, cruel treatment, inhumane, degrading human dignity, and exploitation in employment relationships.
2. Women domestic workers as referred to in paragraph (1) must receive protection from employers in the form of:
a. recognition of rights, wages and decent working conditions;
b. health and social security; and
c. guarantee not to discriminate, inhumane treatment, degrading human dignity, and exploitation.

Paragraph 8

Women Victims of Violence

Article 12

1. Women heads of households as referred to in Article 9 letter b, are widows whose husbands have died and as a result of divorce must receive protection.
2. Implementation of protection for women heads of households as referred to in paragraph (1) in order to provide protection and prevention against forms of discrimination, negative stigma and economic empowerment for women heads of households.
3. Women as heads of households as referred to in paragraph (2) receive protection rights against:
a. discriminatory actions and efforts to weaken the function of women as economic supporters of the family;
b. strengthening capacity and recognition as heads of households in their environment; and
c. accessibility to economic and financial institutions.
4. Implementation of protection for women as heads of households whose husbands have died as referred to in paragraph (1) includes: a. women as heads of households obtain 1/8 (one eighth) of the total remaining assets of their husbands if they have children; and b. women as heads of households obtain 1/4 (one quarter) of the total remaining assets of their husbands if they do not have children.
5. Implementation of protection for women as heads of households as a result of divorce as referred to in paragraph (1) during the iddah period, the former husband is responsible for providing residence and support.

CHAPTER V

PROTECTION OF WOMEN

Part One

Implementation of Protection of Women

CHAPTER IX

STRATEGY AND MECHANISM FOR WOMEN'S PROTECTION

Part One

General

Article 15

1. The implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 9 letter e, in order to provide protection and prevention, against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) receive the right to protection over:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development; b. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and c. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 23

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and empowerment for women victims, the Regency Government may cooperate with the community/community institutions.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 8

1. Every woman who is in a condition of disability, old age, and/or pregnant, has the right to obtain facilities and special treatment related to access to public services.
2. Every elderly woman, person with physical disabilities and/or mental disabilities, has the right to obtain care, education, training, and special assistance at the expense of the Regency Government to ensure a decent life in accordance with human dignity.
3. Every woman who is entangled with narcotics either as a perpetrator or victim has the right to receive fair treatment both in the law enforcement process and the rehabilitation (recovery) process.

2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

Article 19

2. In the event of violence, every victim has the right to receive health services and assistance, both psychologically and legally and to receive guarantees of their rights related to their status as women.

I. GENERAL

1. That Islamic Sharia grants a high and noble position to women. Women have the same position as men as servants of Allah and dignified beings. 2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

General

I. GENERAL

1. That Islamic Sharia grants a high and noble position to women. Women have the same position as men as servants of Allah and dignified beings. In the Al-Qur'an and the Hadith of the Prophet SAW, no teachings and activities have ever been found that lead to discrimination and exploitation of women. In fact, one of the missions of the Prophet SAW in this world is to elevate the dignity and honor of women from a very low and degrading state.
2. That Law Number 44 of 1999 concerning the Implementation of Special Autonomy for Aceh and Law Number 11 of 2006 concerning the Governance of Aceh have provided a foundation for the empowerment and protection of women which is an important activity because the condition of women so far has been quite concerning both in terms of education, economy, health, labor, law and even threats of violence, exploitation, discrimination, pornography and pornographic acts which are often targeted at women.
3. The obligation of the Bireuen Regency Government feels the need to have a Bireuen Regency Qanun on the Empowerment and Protection of Women, it is expected that every woman can be empowered and receive protection without discrimination and also the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) which already exists in Bireuen Regency has a Juridical Foundation as one of the implementers of empowerment and protection of women in Bireuen Regency.

15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Qanun, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bireuen Regency.
2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Qanun, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bireuen Regency.
2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

3. The obligation of the Bireuen Regency Government feels the need to have a Bireuen Regency Qanun on the Empowerment and Protection of Women, it is expected that every woman can be empowered and receive protection without discrimination and also the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) which already exists in Bireuen Regency has a Juridical Foundation as one of the implementers of empowerment and protection of women in Bireuen Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Qanun, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bireuen Regency.
2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2), is carried out within the framework of strengthening synergy in policy formulation, program and activity support, as well as monitoring and evaluation.

1. In implementing policies, programs, and activities for the protection of women and empowerment for women victims, the Regency Government may cooperate with the community/community institutions.
2. Cooperation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IX

AWARDS

Article 36

1. The Regency Government grants awards to State Apparatus who are deemed to have commitment and succeed in carrying out the duties of women's protection.
2. The Regency Government grants awards to Community Organizations, Private Sector and Individuals who are deemed to have made innovations and succeed in supporting women's protection efforts.
3. Awards are also granted to Gampong Governments who are deemed to have commitment and succeed in supporting women's protection efforts.
4. Further regulation regarding the granting of awards as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 40

1. Evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for women's protection is conducted at the end of each fiscal year.
2. The results of the evaluation of the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for women's protection are used as input material for the formulation of policies, programs, and activities for women's protection for the following year.
3. Evaluation as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 27

1. The District Government establishes a women's protection institution.
2. The women's protection institution as referred to in paragraph (1) also handles protection for children.
3. The women's protection institution as referred to in paragraph (2) is implemented by establishing UPTD PPA.
4. The District Government must guarantee the availability of adequate facilities and infrastructure, human resources, and budget to realize the operations of UPTD PPA.
5. Further provisions regarding UPTD PPA are regulated by Regent Regulation.

I. GENERAL

1. That Islamic Sharia grants a high and noble position to women. Women have the same position as men as servants of Allah and dignified beings. In the Al-Qur'an and the Hadith of the Prophet SAW, no teachings and activities have ever been found that lead to discrimination and exploitation of women. In fact, one of the missions of the Prophet SAW in this world is to elevate the dignity and honor of women from a very low and degrading state.
2. That Law Number 44 of 1999 concerning the Implementation of Special Autonomy for Aceh and Law Number 11 of 2006 concerning the Governance of Aceh have provided a foundation for the empowerment and protection of women which is an important activity because the condition of women so far has been quite concerning both in terms of education, economy, health, labor, law and even threats of violence, exploitation, discrimination, pornography and pornographic acts which are often targeted at women.
3. The obligation of the Bireuen Regency Government feels the need to have a Bireuen Regency Qanun on the Empowerment and Protection of Women, it is expected that every woman can be empowered and receive protection without discrimination and also the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) which already exists in Bireuen Regency has a Juridical Foundation as one of the implementers of empowerment and protection of women in Bireuen Regency.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Qanun, what is meant by:

1. Region is Bireuen Regency.
2. Regency is Bireuen Regency which is part of the provincial region of Aceh led by a Regent.
3. Regency Government is the Government of Bireuen Regency as the administration of affairs carried out by the regency government and the Regional House of Representatives of Bireuen Regency in accordance with their respective functions and authorities.
4. Regency Government is an element of the administration of the Regency Government consisting of the Regent and regency apparatus.
5. Regent is the Head of the Government of Bireuen Regency who is elected through a democratic process conducted based on the principles of direct, general, free, secret, honest and fair in accordance with the laws and regulations.
6. Regional House of Representatives of the Regency hereinafter abbreviated as DPRK is an element of the administration of the Government of Bireuen Regency whose members are elected through general elections in accordance with the laws and regulations.
7. Woman is a person (human being) who has reached the age of 15 years who has menstruated, is pregnant, gives birth and breastfeeds.
8. Protection of Women is all efforts aimed at protecting women and providing a sense of security in the fulfillment of their rights by providing consistent and systematic attention aimed at achieving just and equal relations with men.
9. Victim is a woman who experiences threats of violence and or violence inside and or outside the household and or becomes an object of trafficking/exploitation, and or discrimination in all its forms and aspects.
10. Threat of Violence is any act of non-physical abuse by using or not using means unlawfully that can cause danger to the body, life, freedom and human rights of women.
11. Violence is any act against a person, especially women, which results in misery or suffering physically, psychologically, sexually and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion, or deprivation of liberty unlawfully, whether within or outside the scope of the household.
12. Discrimination Against Women is any distinction, exclusion or restriction made on the basis of sex which has the effect or purpose of reducing or eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or exercise of human rights and fundamental freedoms in the political, economic, social, cultural, civil or any other field by women, regardless of their marital status on the basis of equality between men and women.
13. Women's Rights are all rights possessed by every woman which are part of human rights.
14. Special Protection is protection provided to women and children in emergency situations, women and children in conflict with the law, women and children from minority and isolated groups, women and children who are exploited economically and/or sexually, women and children who are trafficked, women and children who are victims of kidnapping, sale, trafficking, women and children victims of violence both physical and/or mental.
15. Society is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations.
16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband-wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
17. Labor Force is every person who is capable of performing work to produce goods and/or services either to meet their own needs or for society.
18. Worker/Laborer is every person who works by receiving wages or remuneration in other forms.
19. Person with Disability is every person who experiences physical, intellectual, mental, and/or sensory limitations in the long term who in interacting with the environment may experience obstacles and difficulties to participate fully and effectively with other citizens based on equal rights.
20. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim when seeing, hearing and knowing that violence against the victim will, is or has occurred.
21. Rehabilitation is a series of actions carried out by authorized parties in their field to restore the physical, mental and psychosocial condition of women to their original condition.

Article 18

1. The implementation of protection for women victims of violence as referred to in Article 9 letter h, in order to provide legal protection and/or health recovery.
2. Protection for women victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) includes:
a. legal aid;
b. assistance after the occurrence of acts of violence;
c. rehabilitation and social reintegration; and
d. health services.

Article 39

1. To ensure synergy, continuity, and effectiveness of integrated measures in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for women's protection, the Regency Government conducts monitoring.
2. Monitoring as referred to in paragraph (1) is intended to determine the progress and obstacles in the implementation of policies, programs, and activities for women's protection.
3. Monitoring is conducted periodically through coordination and direct monitoring of regional apparatus implementing policies, programs and activities for women's protection.
4. Monitoring is conducted from planning to implementation of policies, programs and activities.

Article 30

(1) Women's protection is implemented by integrating Gender Mainstreaming (PUG) and disaggregated databases, gender data and violence data in an integrated manner based on applicable laws and regulations.

(2) The District Work Unit that handles women's empowerment and protection coordinates with other Regional Apparatus Organizations in order to realize the implementation of women's protection in an integrated manner.

(3) Coordination as referred to in paragraph (2), is carried out within the framework of strengthening synergy in policy formulation, program and activity support, as well as monitoring and evaluation.

Part Four

Special Treatment

Article 22

1. The Regency Government has obligations and responsibilities for the protection of women.
2. Efforts to protect women as referred to in paragraph (1) include:
a. determination of policies, programs, and activities;
b. determination of implementation guidelines;
c. provision of services; and
d. coordination of policies, programs and activities.
3. Protection of women as referred to in paragraph (2) is carried out in an integrated manner in accordance with laws and regulations.

Article 8

1. Every woman who is in a condition of disability, old age, and/or pregnant, has the right to obtain facilities and special treatment related to access to public services.
2. Every elderly woman, person with physical disabilities and/or mental disabilities, has the right to obtain care, education, training, and special assistance at the expense of the Regency Government to ensure a decent life in accordance with human dignity.
3. Every woman who is entangled with narcotics either as a perpetrator or victim has the right to receive fair treatment both in the law enforcement process and the rehabilitation (recovery) process.

Article 15

1. The implementation of protection for women with disabilities as referred to in Article 9 letter e, in order to provide protection and prevention, against forms of discrimination including freedom from cruel, inhuman treatment, degrading human dignity, and freedom from exploitation.
2. Women with disabilities as referred to in paragraph (1) receive the right to protection over:
a. guarantee of continuity and personal self-development; b. accessibility of information, legal aid, mobility, social services; and c. early intervention efforts including treatment and rehabilitation to improve their function and capacity.

Article 42

This Qanun shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Qanun is ordered by placing it in the Bireuen Regency Gazette.
